sound: one mora of closure that doubles the following consonant
strokeOrder: begin at the upper left and sweep right across the high shoulder
without lifting, round down the right side and finish by sweeping left along the lower curve
strokeOrderNote: Sirgazil's 24-frame つ animation supplies the one-run order; Unicode 17 identifies U+3063 as the small-tsu letter, so the same movement is fitted to its smaller bundled glyph.

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sirgazil, Hiragana つ stroke order animation.gif, hiragana つ, 24 frames, 2.4 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 1 October 2009); Unicode Standard 17.0 names U+3063 HIRAGANA LETTER SMALL TU, alias small tsu
strokeOrderSource.variation: The CC0 animation draws full-size つ in one uninterrupted run from the upper left, right across the high shoulder, around the descending right side, and back left along the lower curve. Unicode 17 separately identifies U+3063 as small tsu. This learner path therefore preserves the source's zero-lift movement while scaling and fitting it to the bundled Noto Sans JP small っ outline; the cited animation demonstrates つ rather than a separately animated っ, so the size adaptation is explicit rather than presented as independent handwriting evidence.

notes: The sokuon counts as one mora and marks closure before a doubled following consonant, as in ちょっと chotto.
